content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram) are dried legumes native to the Mediterranean, South Asia and Africa. They have a mild nutty flavor, a creamy texture when cooked, and are used in soups, salads, hummus and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas belong to the legume family and are close relatives of beans and peas.
Dried chickpeas can be stored for 2–3 years under proper conditions.
In ancient Egypt chickpeas were a staple food and also used in ritual offerings.
Chickpea flour is gluten‑free and popular for gluten‑free baking.
Chickpeas are one of the most widely used ingredients in Indian cuisine.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas provide about 20 % protein, making them a valuable protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Chickpeas contain folate, thiamine and vitamin B6, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron aids in hemoglobin formation, while magnesium supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Chickpeas raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for diabetes management and weight control.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Phytates
items.content: Phytate content can reduce mineral absorption; soaking chickpeas before cooking helps mitigate this.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes, including chickpeas, can cause bloating in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chickpeas can be boiled, stewed, roasted, ground into flour, or blended into hummus. Before cooking, soak dried chickpeas for at least 8–12 hours, then boil until tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried chickpeas in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored, they keep their quality for 2–3 years.
